messages:
emma_support: FYI Skyward escalated — sustained 429s on their dedicated pool since 06:20 UTC. They report long auth handshakes and large request queueing. Ticket INC-4921.
liam_se: Can you paste the QPS profile? baseline vs peak?
emma_support: baseline ~220 qps steady, but bursted to ~1.15k qps for ~6m around 06:25. Observed 65-90% queue depth.
jana_infra: Which pool size are they on? GPUs / replicas?
emma_support: Pool is 5xA10G, min_replicas=3, max=8, autoscale threshold 0.7 (cpu/gpu util). Warmup_delay=90s.
liam_se: 1.15k QPS on 5 GPUs is very spiky. At 220 baseline that config is fine, but burst overwhelms autoscale window. Was KV/prefix caching enabled?
emma_support: Not for this customer — disabled by default in their config. Also saw auth service 500s -> 1.2s latencies around same window.
mike_customer_success: Customer says billing auth calls spiked around the burst — they did a campaign that hit our token exchange endpoint.
jana_infra: That matches logs: opsbot:alert: auth-proxy rate_limit_exceeded for tenant skyward at 06:24:31 -> returned 429 to runtime.
opsbot: "[ALERT] tenant=skyward service=auth-proxy code=429 count=1245 window=60s"
liam_se: So two amplification issues: auth proxy rate limits -> runtime queues requests -> autoscaler slow to react -> sustained 429s. Also cold KV cache since caching off -> per-request model overhead high.
emma_support: Repro steps in case infra wants to simulate: 1) toggle tenant to no-prefix-cache, 2) run a 10m ramp to 1200 QPS with 5s p95 token sizes, 3) watch auth-proxy tokens/sec and runtime queue.
liam_se: Quick mitigations we can apply now: 1) temporarily increase pool to 9 GPUs (manual scale), 2) lower autoscale threshold to 0.5 and reduce warmup_delay to 20s, 3) enable prefix/KV caching for Skyward, 4) add auth-proxy rate limit backoff to client (CS to notify customer).
jana_infra: I'll apply 1 & 2 now for immediate relief. Emma — can you toggle caching after we scale?
emma_support: On it. Also suggesting per-tenant concurrency cap to stop noisy neighboring tenants from absorbing headroom.
mike_customer_success: I'll ask Skyward to throttle the campaign (small change) and add client-side retry with exponential backoff. They're ok with temporary scale-up.
liam_se: Postmortem action items: - enforce warmup_delay <=30s for bursty tenants, - default prefix caching on for dedicated pools, - add autoscale predictor for scheduled campaigns, - set auth-proxy soft limits with graceful 503 fallback + retry guidance.
jana_infra: Scaling done: pool now 9xA10G, min_replicas bumped. Seeing queue depth drop and 429s tailing off.
opsbot: "[INFO] pool_scale event tenant=skyward from=5 to=9 by=jana_infra ts=2401234822"
emma_support: Skyward confirm 429s drop to <1% and p95 latency improved from 2.4s -> 0.9s. CS will coordinate billing/auth throttling follow-up.
liam_se: For the formal support runbook, adding a short run-repro:```bash
# simulate auth stress + model load
siege -c 1200 -t 6M 'POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate
  Authorization: Bearer <token>'
# monitor auth-proxy logs and runtime queue length
```
emma_support: I'll update the ticket INC-4921 with steps taken, links to logs, and the recommended config changes. Assigning follow-ups to infra and product for defaults. :white_check_mark:
mike_customer_success: Thanks team — customer very appreciative of quick relief.
liam_se: Leaving note: consider autoscale pre-warm for scheduled marketing campaigns (feature request).
opsbot: "[NOTE] incident-resolved suggestion added to INC-4921 by liam_se"
